spec.name: assay-verdict
spec.intent:
Worktree /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share (branch design/first-share); every path below is under it and no command runs in the main checkout. Census @f2cd7e3a: the design was corrected there; plan architect-position is stopped under `design stability` and its landed architect-role and architect-skills work (7d53132e, e944facb, 9809add3, c076a864, ce240336, 539140df) is this unit's starting state. Re-derive any count or line below if a listed path changed since. Realize `assay verdict`: the assayer's judgement of one unit against the design shard it was created to realize, achieved or not achieved with what is missing, naming the unit and its implementer, stated in the design's own language; the assayer holds the design and never the unit's spec, so the verdict is a second, independent description, and acceptance rests on it, not on the implementer's account. At census the assayer is built to NOT judge: packages/canon/src/dimensions/role/assayer.ts says `¬emits ⟨verdict ⟨accept ∉ remit ∵ keyed-to C ⟨amended-by design-holder⟩⟩ · …⟩`; agents/assayer.ts's description says 'Returns CONCEPTS, never a verdict: it does not accept, reject …' and its archetype 'leaving the decision to the party that owns the design … an accept or a reject takes a decision that was never delegated'; its header comment says 'the VERDICT stays with the design-holder'; roles/assayer.ts's comment says 'judging is not its remit'. The three questions a verdict answers live today only in deliver's formal block (`achieved(unit) ⇔ realizes(unit) ∈ assay(artifact(unit)) ∧ spells ∧ covers ∧ sole`), a skill the assayer does not hold.
THE LOOP (the contract the workflow units of this plan each state their own share of; the shards say what must hold, this is how). (1) The architect cuts a shard and dispatches the planner with it; the planner plans it and, when no plan is bound, binds it, returning only the plan's name. (2) The architect dispatches one integrator for the bound plan, named for the plan and kept warm across its waves where the harness can message a finished delegate (Claude Code: SendMessage to the name given at dispatch; omp: agent messaging); the integrator records each ready unit active as it hands out its address and returns only addresses, `<unit> of <plan>`. (3) The architect dispatches one implementer per address, naming the delegate after the unit and giving it the address and nothing it wrote itself. The implementer reads its spec, builds on its own branch, runs only its unit's own checks, commits its own work, and returns only `landed <unit> of <plan> at <commit>`, or `blocked <unit> of <plan>: spec` when the spec cannot be built as written (the architect routes that address to the planner). Its account of the work stays out of the return; what it doubts or meets beside the path it captures as a note. (4) The architect dispatches the assayer with the address and commit. The assayer reads the shard the unit realizes and the files at that commit, never the spec, and returns the assay verdict: achieved, or not achieved with what is missing in the design's own words, naming the unit and its implementer. (5) Not achieved: the architect sends the findings to the same implementer by the name it gave it, and the unit returns to (4). Achieved: the architect hands the address and commit to the integrator. (6) The integrator combines the unit onto the plan's integration line (a branch cut from main when the plan is bound, `plan/<plan>`) and runs the project's whole check once on the combined tree; no implementer or assayer runs it. Green: it records the unit completed, commits the records written since (plan, design, notes) by pathspec, and returns the unit as whole with the newly ready addresses. Red or a merge conflict: it leaves the line as it was and returns `red <unit> of <plan>: <failing check>`, which the architect sends to the same implementer. It never repairs, never reads to judge, and decides nothing. (7) When every unit is completed and the whole holds, the integrator closes the plan and asks the operator to release the line to main: a pull request where the repository has a forge remote and `gh`, otherwise the exact git command. It never moves main. (8) The architect never runs `plan show <unit>`, and never reads a spec, a diff, an artifact or an implementer's account; it runs no check and makes no commit or merge. Unit names reach it only as addresses, from the integrator and on verdicts. (9) Design stability. Every input, whether from the operator, a delegate or the architect itself, is a hypothesis the architect rectifies against its expertise and industry practice. A surviving change that bears on a shard the bound plan realizes is captured as a decision note on that concept's topic, blocking nothing; it is amended into the design only after that plan closes, and a following plan realizes it. A change to a concept no bound plan realizes is amended at once. Only when the architect finds the bound plan built on a shard that is itself wrong does it stop the plan: it captures a note blocking the plan (an owed ruling, so no unit is ready), corrects the shard once, and the planner rectifies the plan (repin, revise, retract, add) or rebuilds it; the architect then retracts the note and work resumes.
CHANGE. (1) packages/canon/src/dimensions/role/assayer.ts: the assayer emits the verdict of (4): per unit, achieved, or not achieved with each missing part as ⟨concept, uncovered factor or clause of the shard, locus as an address⟩, naming the unit and its implementer. The three questions move here from deliver: does the artifact spell its concept's anchor, does its behaviour cover the shard exactly (nothing missing, nothing extra; an extra is a second concept smuggled in), and does anything else already realize it. It reads the shard (`design show <concept>`) and the files at the commit it is given, never `plan show <unit>` or any spec, and never the implementer's account. Keep the prohibition on mechanism-prose (naming, structure, test quality as opinions); a missing part is stated in the shard's words.
(2) packages/canon/src/roles/assayer.ts: rewrite the comments that say judging is not its remit; skills stay ['design']. outputFormat structured-data holds (the verdict is a record, not a narrative).
(3) packages/canon/src/agents/assayer.ts: description and archetype state that it returns the verdict, with the header comment's 'the VERDICT stays with the design-holder' rewritten; it is still not a reviewer (no opinion on mechanism, no recommendation), and its verdict is on the unit against its shard, never on the whole line.
(4) .changeset/assay-verdict.md (@cratylus/canon minor).
deliver's copy of the three questions is removed by wave-1 unit deliver-loop, which cites the assayer's. No new test file.
